purpose: Date the historical Eastern Fleet heavy-group movement and convert it into evidence gates without back-porting those future historical observations into Branch-B realized 1944 state.

sources.title: Vice Admiral Eastern Fleet War Diary, 15 Dec 1943-31 Jan 1944
sources.note: Detailed day-by-day passage chronology; transcription of Admiralty war diary.

sources.title: Royal Navy Historical Branch, Naval War Diary January 1944
sources.note: Official diary index/January station planning; used as corroboration, not required for Branch realization.

historical_events.event: Renown leaves Rosyth for Scapa after foreign-service preparation
Renown, Queen Elizabeth and Valiant sail Scapa; carriers depart Clyde later same night
Heavy ships and carriers assemble west of Skerryvore and shape course south/west for Gibraltar
Battleship group arrives Gibraltar and fuels under secrecy precautions
historical_events.intelligence_note: Night passage and precautions reduce neutral visual reporting reliability; do not auto-promote Japanese confidence.

historical_events.event: Carrier group passes Europa Point; battleship group sails Gibraltar 04:15 and reunites east of the Strait
War diary records Group A and nearby convoy probably sighted by enemy aircraft
War diary records German aircraft sighting of the force
historical_events.intelligence_note: This is the first source-grounded robust external visual gate. Whether/when the report reaches Japanese decision channels remains a Branch event.

historical_events.event: Group A off Port Said; Canal transit begins
Renown and carriers in Suez Bay; Queen Elizabeth and Valiant join
Force departs Suez eastbound through Red Sea
Aden fueling in two heavy-ship groups because of harbour/tide limits
Renown reaches Colombo; long-range Ceylon aircraft have already contacted/shadowed the force
Queen Elizabeth, Valiant and Illustrious reach Trincomalee; Group A passage complete
Queen Elizabeth and Valiant undertake deferred boiler cleaning/normal defect repair; Renown follows after early-Feb arrival Trincomalee
historical_events.intelligence_note: Arrival is not identical to immediate battle-ready eastbound sortie.

historical_events.event: First Battle Squadron intended to resume squadron training at sea

working_detection_interpretation.pre_1944-01-10: Growing but non-decisive indicators only. Gibraltar secrecy measures explicitly prevent treating port passage as automatic Japanese high confidence.
working_detection_interpretation.1944-01-10: Possible enemy-air sighting raises confidence but report identity and dissemination remain uncertain.
working_detection_interpretation.1944-01-11: German visual sighting is sufficient source evidence for a HIGH-confidence eastbound assessment if the report is delivered to Japanese operational intelligence in a useful time window.
working_detection_interpretation.after_1944-01-12: Port Said/Suez/Aden stages progressively remove ambiguity, but later confirmation may arrive too late to maximize a 6-8 day Truk release clock.

working_release_policy.decision_rule: Do not issue a realized GO from historical hindsight alone. First adjudicate Axis-to-Japan report delivery. Timely receipt of the 11 Jan German visual report is sufficient to cross the working HIGH-confidence release threshold unless a new Pacific emergency blocks release.
working_release_policy.movement_clock: 6-8 days center from Truk mobile pool to Singapore/Lingga via Palau and Balikpapan/Tarakan fuel gate
working_release_policy.second_gate: Do not infer immediate RN eastbound combat sortie from Ceylon arrival; branch must separately adjudicate repair/training/readiness and any actual sortie.

branch_realization.RN_future_Suez_Aden_Ceylon_events: historical trace baseline only until their clocks are reached; do not instantiate early

next_gate: Run Jan13-20 parallel movement/detection clock. RN Group A continues from Suez toward Aden on historical trace unless a Branch event interrupts; Japanese surface release departs Truk on its own clock. Update Allied inference from observables rather than hindsight.
